newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey agrees gas purchases from Turkmenistan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey agrees gas purchases from Turkmenistan.

text.p: Turkey will buy up to eight billion cubic metres of natural gas annually from Turkmenistan from the year 2000, Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan said on Monday.
"All technical studies will be completed by February 15, 1997 according to the gas agreement signed with Turkmenistan," Kutan said in a statement.

"Physical investments will begin by June, 1997 at the latest," he said after arriving back from a four-day visit to Tehran, where he met Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh and Turkmen Deputy Prime Minister Batyr Sardjaev.

He said Turkmen gas would be transported to Turkey after Iran and Turkey completed sections of a pipeline from Tabriz to the eastern Turkish city of Erzurum as part of a giant gas deal signed between Ankara and Tehran in August.
"Turkmen gas will reach Tabriz through existing pipelines. It will later reach Erzurum through the pipeline to be built from Tabriz to Turkey," Kutan said.

Turkey agreed with Iran in August to get three billion cubic metres of Iranian gas from 1998 through a pipeline whose construction is scheduled to begin in March, 1997. The pipeline will first be built from Tabriz to the eastern Turkish city of Erzurum and later to Ankara.

The 23-year, $23-billion agreement envisages that Iran and Turkey build the sections of the pipeline on their territories. Turkey's gas purchases will be raised to 10 billion cubic metres a year from 2005.
Ministers from the three countries will meet in March in Ashgabat for a review of the project, Kutan said.

Kutan also said a feasibility study for a project to carry Iranian crude oil to Western markets through a pipeline via Turkey's southern Ceyhan terminal. The two countries will come together on January 15 to discuss details of the project.
